summary.headline: Dynamic Cables Q4 FY26 revenue growth slowed to 7% YoY (core products ~20%), with a greenfield plant delayed to September 2026 and order book at INR808 crores.
summary.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue (up 17% YoY), operating profit up 23% to INR130 crores at a 10.8% margin, and PAT up 30% to INR84 crores. Q4 overall growth was only 7% because low-value LV conductors and railway signalling cables were discontinued, while core products grew about 20%. The greenfield capacity has slipped roughly 15 months versus earlier guidance and is now targeted to start production around September 2026. Order book stood at INR808 crores at 31 March 2026, with management attributing softer March order booking to aluminium and PVC price spikes.

financial_highlights.change: Realisation growth 12%, volume growth 8% for core products
Management cited ~11% YoY growth (analyst figure; ~18% also cited)
Lower YoY per analyst; management steered to operating margin
Down from INR66 crores; net debt rose QoQ on seasonal working capital

segments.name: Product mix FY26
segments.commentary: HV cable 64%, LV cable 30%, conductor 6% of FY26 sales. Railway signalling cable was zero in FY26 versus 4% in FY25; LV conductors fell below 5% of sales from 8-9% a year earlier.

segments.name: Customer mix FY26
segments.commentary: Private 80%, Government 13%, Export 7% of FY26 sales. Export declined slightly in FY26 and March 2026 exports were nil.

segments.name: Solar cables
segments.commentary: About 18% of FY26 sales versus INR105 crores (10%) in FY25; management expects a 20-23% share in FY27. Margins in line with company average.

segments.name: Cables vs conductors
segments.commentary: Cables volume grew about 18% in FY26 and high single digits in Q4; conductors degrew sharply (50-60% volume decline in low-cost conductors).

guidance_outlook: No short-term or yearly guidance given; long-term growth guidance of 18-20% (value terms, multi-year) reiterated, with ~1.5x industry growth expected in FY27 ('should be able to do it').
New greenfield plant targeted to go live around September 2026, with trial production in next 3-4 months; no firm date given. Capacity to be available ahead of the seasonally stronger H2 FY27.
H1 FY27 growth to be managed from existing facilities; management said current capacity is sufficient for H1 order book.

Peak turnover capacity guided at about INR135 crores per month (set before the recent commodity price rise); optimal utilisation 85-90%. Asset turn guided at about 6x (conservative 5x for the INR40 crore capex).
Export share targeted at 10% long term and 15% in the medium to long term; US re-entry restarted after tariff disruption.
Operating margin guided at 10.5-11% through the year, delivered in FY26.
capex_capacity: Greenfield plant delayed roughly 15 months versus Q2 FY26 target due to regulatory approvals, freight disruption for imported machinery (linked to the Iran war), and AERB compliance requirements.
Most machinery and civil work now done; trial production expected in about 3-4 months, with commercial start targeted for September 2026.
Further capex expected each year to sustain growth, but not as intense as FY26; next capex set not yet crystallised. FY26 capex was high due to the greenfield plant.

TS Conductor tie-up (carbon core HTLS conductors) needs little incremental capex as existing facilities can be used; no hard revenue timeline, with type testing and approvals expected to take about a year.
Utilisation was 75-80% in Q3 FY26 and management described it as around 85-90% at present. Capacity is fungible across products.
demand_pricing: Aluminium and PVC prices spiked in March 2026; management says customers deferred orders, but acceptance is gradually building and grid-driven demand cannot be deferred for long.
Realisation growth was 12% in Q4 and about 8% for FY26, with the balance from volume; price variation clauses pass most raw material costs through, while firm-price orders are hedged at booking.
Railway signalling cables discontinued due to high competitive intensity and low margins; capacity redirected to power cables.
Data centre cable development is at a very early stage; no quarterly update given.
US business restarting after a 6-8 month gap caused by tariffs; distributor-led market and some contribution expected in FY27 with the size not yet quantifiable.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 growth came from volume versus realisation, and why is growth soft?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall Q4 growth was 7%, but core products grew about 20%; the gap reflects discontinued LV conductors and railway cables. Realisation grew 12% and volume 8% for core products. The high Q4 FY25 base (38-39% growth) and March order deferrals also weighed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 growth outlook given the capex delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated that it does not give yearly guidance and that long-term growth is 18-20%. H1 FY27 is to be served from existing capacity, with the new plant targeted for September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the greenfield plant slip?
qa_highlights.answer: Three causes: delayed regulatory approvals, imported machinery shipments delayed by freight issues after the Iran war, and AERB compliance requirements. Management now says most machinery and civil work is done.

qa_highlights.question: What happened to gross margin and other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin varies with product, customer and freight mix and steered analysts to operating margin, which was steady at the 10.5-11% guided range. Employee cost decline was attributed to a one-time Q4 FY25 bonus accrual.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TS Conductor tie-up and what does it mean for revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an entry step into the high-voltage conductor market using carbon core HTLS technology, mainly for the domestic market. Product approvals and type testing take about a year, and there is no hard revenue timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 capacity be enough, and what is the next capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is fungible across products. Next capex is not yet decided, but incremental capex is directionally expected to sustain growth.

risks_watch: Greenfield plant timing: trial production and a September 2026 start depend on site progress and imported machinery freight, with repeated delays already.
Raw material volatility: aluminium and PVC spikes could continue to defer orders and affect margins, especially in H1 FY27 when capacity is tight.
Working capital and debt: net debt rose QoQ in March, and management says finance costs will not rise, but this needs monitoring.
Order book momentum: order book growth of about 11-18% YoY (figures varied on the call) lags the 18-20% long-term target.
Export recovery and US re-entry timing remain unquantified; export fell slightly in FY26.
Management commentary was repeatedly evasive on quarterly gross margin changes and on the FY27 growth outlook.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand and margins, but cautious and often evasive on near-term items: quarterly gross margin, FY27 guidance, the plant go-live date, and next capex. Repeatedly deflected analyst questions to operating margin and to long-term 18-20% growth.

We have always been giving a long-term guidance of 18% to 20% growth, which we have also delivered in the past and we still believe that for a medium to long term, the company will deliver the same kind of growth in future also.

There is no definitive date, but yes, we are kind of guiding that based on the developments at the site level, at the plant level, we should be able to go live by September.

adds.what: Greenfield cable plant (capex INR40 crore), peak turnover capacity ~INR135 crore/month when fully running

growth.why: Long-term guidance of 18-20% value growth is reiterated, backed by order book of INR808 crore, 85% utilisation and a greenfield plant (INR40 crore) targeted for September 2026, but the plant has slipped about 15 months and Q4 revenue growth was only 7%.
